alignments.note: Anarthrous participle takes the supplied 'Whoso' (rule 46), headed on the lexeme. Variant WLC.PSA.101.5.v001 is underdetermined with the base reading retained and compatible with the ASV; no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so nothing is added or unrepresented on its account.

Privily jointly renders the preposition and secrecy noun under rules 30 and 40. The comparison with hayyom was considered, but this adverb expresses covert slander without the definite reference carried by to day.
The article's determination is not expressed by privily; lack of a separate English word alone does not authorize its fusion (rules 12, 29 and 30).
Object marker; the resumptive 'him' is the suffix's (rule 16).

Construct adjective 'high (of eyes)' keeps its own 'high'. The fronted 'Him' is given to the resumptive object suffix on the second אֵת (s016) under rule 11's priority of a present pronominal morpheme over a supplied substantival pronoun, so the adjective takes no supplied 'Him' under rule 46; the competing reading gives 'Him' to this adjective as its rule-46 noun phrase and leaves s016 unrepresented, which was the earlier alignment.

Supplied relative and verb of having make the construct adjective into a relative clause; one added unit as in rule 2's טוֹב־עַיִן → 'He that hath a bountiful eye'. No הָיָה, יֵשׁ, or possessive preposition stands in the clause to carry the 'hath' (rule 43).
'eyes' recast as 'a look'; the supplied 'a' joins the noun (rule 15).
'wide of heart' rendered 'proud heart'; the adjective keeps its own word.

Resumptive 3ms object suffix realized by the fronted 'Him' (rules 18, 25), exactly as the first colon's אוֹתוֹ takes 'him'; the ASV fronts the object and writes it once, and a present pronominal morpheme takes the pronoun before a supplied substantival reading does (rule 11). Competing reading: 'Him' as the rule-46 supplied pronoun of גְּבַהּ, leaving this suffix unrepresented.
יכל 'be able' rendered 'suffer' (tolerate) with its own auxiliary and subject pronoun; the negative keeps a separate 'not', so no 'cannot' fusion (rule 35).
